arxiv-2102-07391.title: Strong decays of the low-lying bottom strange baryons
arxiv-2102-07391.creator: Hui-Zhen He, Wei Liang, Qi-Fang Lü, Yu-Bing Dong
arxiv-2102-07391.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Hui-Zhen He, Wei Liang, Qi-Fang Lü, Yu-Bing Dong. In this work, the strong decay behaviors of the λ − \lambda- mode low-lying Ξ b \Xi_{b} and Ξ b ′ \Xi_{b}^{\prime} baryons are investigated within the P 0 3 {}^{3}P_{0} model.

arxiv-2203-10137.title: Optimal Dose-Limited Phase Estimation without Entanglement
arxiv-2203-10137.creator: Stewart A. Koppell, Mark A. Kasevich
arxiv-2203-10137.description: Abstract Phase estimation is one of the central themes of quantum metrology, with applications in sensing, microscopy, and quantum computation. When estimating a phase shift in a lossy medium, there is an upper bound on the attainable information per probe particle particle sent through the phase shifting element. Previously, only entanglement-enhanced measurements have been shown to saturate this bound.

arxiv-2205-14463.title: Deep VLBI Observations Challenge Previous Evidence of a Binary Supermassive Black Hole Residing in the Seyfert Galaxy NGC 7674 Facilities: VLBA, EVN, VLA astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2018 ) , CASA, AIPS
arxiv-2205-14463.creator: Peter Breiding, Sarah Burke-Spolaor, Tao An, Karishma Bansal, Prashanth Mohan, Gregory B. Taylor, Yingkang Zhang
arxiv-2205-14463.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Peter Breiding, Sarah Burke-Spolaor, Tao An, Karishma Bansal, Prashanth Mohan, Gregory B. Taylor, Yingkang Zhang. Previous Ku-band (15 GHz) imaging with data obtained from the Very Long Baseline Array (VLBA) had shown two compact, sub-pc components at the location of a presumed kpc-scale radio core in the Seyfert galaxy NGC 7674. It was then presumed that these two unresolved and compact components were dual radio cores corresponding to two supermassive black holes (SMBHs) accreting surrounding gas and launching radio-bright relativistic jets.

arxiv-2304-10896.title: GCNH: A Simple Method For Representation Learning On Heterophilous Graphs
arxiv-2304-10896.creator: Andrea Cavallo 1 2 , Claas Grohnfeldt 2 , Michele Russo 2 , Giulio Lovisotto 2 and Luca Vassio 1
arxiv-2304-10896.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Andrea Cavallo 1 2 , Claas Grohnfeldt 2 , Michele Russo 2 , Giulio Lovisotto 2 and Luca Vassio 1. Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are well-suited for learning on homophilous graphs, i.e., graphs in which edges tend to connect nodes of the same type. Yet, achievement of consistent GNN performance on heterophilous graphs remains an open research problem. Recent works have proposed extensions to standard GNN architectures to improve performance on heterophilous graphs, trading off model simplicity for prediction accuracy.

arxiv-2405-06453.title: Searching for linear structures in the failure of the Stone-Weierstrass theorem
arxiv-2405-06453.creator: Marc Caballer, Sheldon Dantas, Daniel L. Rodríguez-Vidanes
arxiv-2405-06453.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Marc Caballer, Sheldon Dantas, Daniel L. Rodríguez-Vidanes. We investigate the failure of the Stone-Weierstrass theorem focusing on the existence of large dimensional vector spaces within the set 𝒞 ⁡ ( L , 𝕂 ) ∖ 𝒜 ¯ \mathcal{C}(L,\mathbb{K})\setminus\overline{\mathcal{A}} , where L L is a compact Hausdorff space and 𝒜 \mathcal{A} is a self-adjoint subalgebra of 𝒞 ⁡ ( L , 𝕂 ) \mathcal{C}(L,\mathbb{K}) that vanishes nowhere on L L but does not necessarily separate the points of L L .

arxiv-2407-07531.title: Beyond Benchmarking: A New Paradigm for Evaluation and Assessment of Large Language Models
arxiv-2407-07531.creator: Jin Liu, Qingquan Li, Wenlong Du
arxiv-2407-07531.description: Abstract In current benchmarks for evaluating large language models (LLMs), there are issues such as evaluation content restriction, untimely updates, and lack of optimization guidance. In this paper, we propose a new paradigm for the measurement of LLMs: Benchmarking-Evaluation-Assessment. Our paradigm shifts the “location” of LLM evaluation from the “examination room” to the “hospital”.

arxiv-2507-10866.title: Quorum sensing of light-activated colloids in nematic liquid crystals
arxiv-2507-10866.creator: Antonio Tavera-Vázquez, David Martin, Haijie Ren, Sam Rubin, Andrés Córdoba, Rui Zhang, Vincenzo Vitelli, Juan J. de Pablo
arxiv-2507-10866.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Antonio Tavera-Vázquez, David Martin, Haijie Ren, Sam Rubin, Andrés Córdoba, Rui Zhang, Vincenzo Vitelli, Juan J. de Pablo. Motile living organisms routinely probe their surroundings to adapt in ever-evolving environments. Although synthetic microswimmers offer surrogates for self-propelled living entities, they often lack the complex feedback mechanisms that enable organisms to adapt.

arxiv-2507-18220.title: Sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics with library optimization mechanism: Recursive long-term prediction perspective
arxiv-2507-18220.creator: Ansei Yonezawa, Heisei Yonezawa, Shuichi Yahagi, Itsuro Kajiwara, Shinya Kijimoto, Hikaru Taniuchi, Kentaro Murakami
arxiv-2507-18220.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ansei Yonezawa, Heisei Yonezawa, Shuichi Yahagi, Itsuro Kajiwara, Shinya Kijimoto, Hikaru Taniuchi, Kentaro Murakami. The sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics (SINDy) approach can discover the governing equations of dynamical systems based on measurement data, where the dynamical model is identified as the sparse linear combination of the given basis functions. A major challenge in SINDy is the design of a library, which is a set of candidate basis functions, as the appropriate library is not trivial for many dynamical systems.

Affiliation: UMONS - Université de Mons Mons
arxiv-2509-14091.creator: Sougata Bose, Daniel Hausmann, Soumyajit Paul, Sven Schewe, Tansholpan Zhanabekova
arxiv-2509-14091.description: Abstract Classic reachability games on graphs are zero-sum games, where the goal of one player, 𝖤𝗏𝖾 {\mathsf{Eve}} , is to visit a vertex from a given target set, and that of other player, 𝖠𝖽𝖺𝗆 {\mathsf{Adam}} , is to prevent this.

arxiv-2601-19086.title: A Leader-Follower Approach for The Attitude Synchronization of Multiple Rigid Body Systems on S ​ O ​ ( 3 ) SO(3)
arxiv-2601-19086.creator: Yiliang Li, Jun-e Feng, Abdelhamid Tayebi
arxiv-2601-19086.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Yiliang Li, Jun-e Feng, Abdelhamid Tayebi. This paper deals with the leader-follower attitude synchronization problem for a group of heterogeneous rigid body systems on S ​ O ​ ( 3 ) SO(3) under an undirected, connected, and acyclic graph communication topology. The proposed distributed control strategy, endowed with almost global asymptotic stability guarantees, allows the synchronization of the rigid body systems to a constant desired orientation known only to a single rigid body.

arxiv-2602-21213.title: Topological Relational Theory: A Simplicial-Complex View of Functional Dependencies, Lossless Decomposition, and Acyclicity
arxiv-2602-21213.creator: Bilge Senturk, Faruk Alpay
arxiv-2602-21213.description: Abstract We develop a topological lens on relational schema design by encoding functional dependencies (FDs) as simplices of an abstract simplicial complex. This dependency complex exposes multi-attribute interactions and allows the use of homological invariants (Betti numbers) to diagnose cyclic dependency structure.

pmc-10734571.creator: Faith M Williams
pmc-10734571.description: These are my personal reflections on the history of approaches to understanding dermal toxicology brought together for the Paton Prize Award. This is not a comprehensive account of all publications from in vivo studies in humans to development of in vitro and in silico approaches but highlghts important progress.

pmc-12800805.title: Translating Cardiovascular Clinical Practice Guidelines on Nutrition Therapy: Validation of the Portfolio Diet Toolkit for Healthcare Providers
pmc-12800805.creator: Gabrielle Viscardi, Sahba Eskandari, Alyssa Chen, Nicholas Chiang, Meaghan E Kavanagh, Songhee Back, Micheal Vallis, Mary J Scourboutakos, Vasanti S Malik, Cyril WC Kendall, David JA Jenkins, John L Sievenpiper, Laura Chiavaroli
pmc-12800805.description: BackgroundCardiovascular disease (CVD) remains a leading cause of death in Canada. Although the Portfolio Diet, a dietary pattern of cholesterol-lowering foods, is supported by CVD clinical practice guidelines, its uptake in clinical practice remains limited. This study assessed the content and face validity of a healthcare provider (HCP)-facing toolkit (infographic and video), designed to support implementation of the Portfolio Diet.

pmc-12954726.title: The Systematic Psychodynamic Multidimensional Organizational Assessment Questionnaire: Protocol for a Development and Validation Study
pmc-12954726.creator: Anne-Maria Müller, Sophia Sachs, Yannik Rieder, Claas Lahmann, Javad Sarvestan
pmc-12954726.description: BackgroundSystems psychodynamics provide valuable insights into organizational development. However, to date, instruments that can reliably assess organizations based on systems psychodynamic theories are scarce. The Systematic Multidimensional Organizational Assessment (SyMOA) is a qualitative instrument that provides an in-depth systems psychodynamic analysis of organizational dynamics using a semistructured interview guide.

pmc-12986804.title: The Comparison of Fresh and Dry Duckweed (Lemna minor L.) on Metal (Cr6+, Cd2+, and Zn2+) Removal from Wastewater
pmc-12986804.creator: Rahin Islam, Noah Smith, Ben Jang, Lin Guo
pmc-12986804.description: Heavy metals contaminating the environment is a global concern. Duckweed (Lemna minor) is a promising plant for the phytoremediation and biosorption of metal-contaminated water. Although studies have shown that duckweed can remove multiple metals, there is limited research comparing the efficiency of fresh and dried biomass for wastewater treatment.

pmc-13059055.title: Elevating Haloperoxidase Expression in Escherichia coli through Fusion with a Formate Oxidase
pmc-13059055.creator: Angelique Pothuizen, Jacob M A van Hengst, Ron Wever, Peter-Leon Hagedoorn, Frank Hollmann
pmc-13059055.description: Vanadium–dependent haloperoxidases (VHPOs) are attractive biocatalysts for halofunctionalisation chemistry, but their routine use is frequently constrained by poor soluble recombinant expression. Here, we explore protein fusion as a construct‐level strategy to simultaneously improve soluble expression of the vanadium chloroperoxidase from Curvularia inaequalis (CiVCPO) and enable in situ H2O2 generation via formate oxidase from Aspergillus oryzae (AoFOx).

pmc-13219545.title: Phytochemical engineering of vanadium pentoxide nanoparticles via neem extract: a sustainable platform for dual in vitro antidiabetic and anticancer activity
pmc-13219545.creator: P. Naveen, Gopi Mamidi, Indira Priyadarsini Amancharla
pmc-13219545.description: This study reports a sustainable green synthesis of vanadium pentoxide nanoparticles (V2O5 NPs) using Azadirachta indica (neem) leaf extract as a natural reducing and stabilizing agent. The formation of V2O5 nanoparticles was confirmed through UV–Vis, FTIR, XRD, SEM, TEM, and zeta potential analyses.

pmc-13303400.title: Immunosuppressive Tumor Microenvironment Signatures Predict Early Progression in NSCLC Patients Receiving Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors: A Transcriptomic and Immune Deconvolution Analysis of GSE135222
pmc-13303400.creator: Hilmi Kodaz, Çağnur Elpen Kodaz, Gökhan Öztürk, İsmail Beypınar
pmc-13303400.description: Background and Objectives: Early progression (PFS < 90 days) in NSCLC patients undergoing ICI treatment constitutes a significant clinical challenge. Although predictive biomarkers have been extensively investigated, specific transcriptomic and immune microenvironment characteristics contributing to early progression remain inadequately characterized. Materials and Methods: We analyzed RNA-seq data from 27 NSCLC patients receiving anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy (GSE135222).

pmc-13354097.title: HIV capsid inhibitors: Mechanisms, resistance, and therapeutic advances
pmc-13354097.creator: Mohamed Mahdi, Botond Lakatos, János András Mótyán, Gyula Hoffka, József Tőzsér
pmc-13354097.description: The capsid (CA) of the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) has emerged as a critical therapeutic target owing to its essential roles in viral replication, nuclear import, and integration. Capsid inhibitors (CIs) disrupt these processes by binding to highly conserved structural interfaces, offering a novel mechanism distinct from enzyme-targeting antiretrovirals.
